research.job_description_summary: Intel hires students and freshers in India as Graduate Technical Interns and, per a May 2026 FACE Prep guide, as Software Development, Hardware Validation and Embedded Software Engineers. The guide describes an online aptitude test, an online technical test (C/C++, DSA, OS, networks, DBMS; digital logic and architecture for ECE/EEE), an optional group discussion and an HR interview. Three 2026 Glassdoor reviews of Graduate Technical Intern interviews describe resume shortlisting by teams and a 45 to 60 minute technical interview on projects, C++, OOP, OS, networks and cryptography. The official careers page was not fetched.
limitations: Intel's official careers page was not fetched, so no round is marked DOCUMENTED.
The FACE Prep guide (2026-05-07) cites no candidate sources and gives no actual questions; it is used as topic context (class D).

Candidate-attributed material is three Glassdoor reviews (January, February and March 2025 interviews, posted February to April 2026) for Graduate Technical Intern; they give project and fundamentals topics. Items based on them carry one report each and are unverified. One review does not state a country.
A 2023 Graduate Engineer Trainee account (electronics basics) is older than the 2025 cutoff and was used only as context.
The Embedded and Software Engineer (Fresher) track is inferred from the guide and has no direct candidate reports; its content is original practice.
Group discussion is described as optional and not held in every drive.

Evidence handling: practice questions cite no sources; where a source only supplied topic context it is named in the question notes. Practice and job-description-inferred questions are UNVERIFIED and capped at LOW confidence on import.

Review status: answers, samples and cited counts come from the researcher and were not independently re-run; spot checks only. Source titles and some dates are blank because the sources did not show them.
Source pages on LeetCode Discuss and Glassdoor returned HTTP 403 to the CodeArena audit tool (2026-10-11), so the cited questions were not re-confirmed against those pages.
